Prefer rotationDelta, which bends the bone relative to its rest orientation; plain rotation replaces the local rotation outright and needs the rest orientation to already be known.

discovery.summary: Edit an Animation Blueprint graph: blend, cached-pose and slot nodes, state machines, states, transitions and transition rules, blend trees.
whenToUse: edit=add_blend_node: Graph needs a blend node.

edit=add_slot_node: Montage slot must be exposed.
edit=create_state_machine: State-driven animation is needed.
edit=add_state_machine: A state machine must be embedded.
edit=add_state: A new animation state is needed.
edit=add_transition: States must connect.
edit=set_transition_rules: Transition condition must change.
edit=set_transition_rules: A state machine must actually be able to leave a state: author the condition here after add_transition.
edit=delete_transition: A transition was authored between the wrong two states.
edit=delete_transition: A transition is dead weight and its rule graph should go with it.
edit=create_blend_tree: Several animations must be switchable through one blend node in an AnimBlueprint.
whenNotToUse: edit=add_cached_pose: Inline pose suffices.
edit=add_slot_node: Use create_montage.

blueprintPath.description: Animation Blueprint whose AnimGraph is edited.

positionX.description: Graph X position of the new node (default 0).

positionY.description: Graph Y position of the new node (default 0).

save.description: Save the asset to disk after the change (default true). With false the change stays in memory only and is lost when the editor restarts.

slotName.description: Slot name.

groupName.description: Slot group the slot belongs to (default DefaultGroup).

transitions.description: Transitions to create between the listed states, as [{ sourceState, targetState }].

stateMachineName.description: Target state machine name inside the Animation Blueprint.

animations.description: Animation asset paths to play in this state; one Sequence Player is created per entry and the first drives the state Result pose. Without it the state is created empty and the character holds its reference pose.

crossfadeDuration.description: Transition blend duration in seconds. blendTime is accepted as an alias.

priorityOrder.description: Evaluation order when several transitions out of one state can fire on the same frame; the lowest wins.

automaticRule.description: Fire the transition when the source state's sequence player reaches the end of its animation instead of testing a condition. Left alone when omitted.

bidirectional.description: Whether the transition also applies from toState back to fromState. Left alone when omitted.

conditionVariable.description: Animation Blueprint variable the transition rule tests, e.g. Speed or bFalling. Without it the rule graph is left unconnected, which reads as false forever and the state machine never leaves its entry state.

conditionComparison.description: How conditionVariable is tested: greater (default), less, greater_equal, less_equal for a numeric variable; true or false for a bool.

conditionValue.description: Right-hand value for a numeric conditionComparison (default 0). Ignored for true/false.

name.description: Name for the created asset or actor.

treeName.description: Comment/name for the blend node (alias of name).

connectToOutput.description: Wire the blend node into the AnimGraph output pose (default true).

edit.description: Which edit anim graph variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

animationsApplied.description: One entry per created Sequence Player. Only the first can be connected to the state Result pose.

animationsFailed.description: Requested animation paths that could not be loaded.

condition.description: The rule that was written into the transition graph. Absent means no conditionVariable was given, so the transition stays false and the state is never left.

deleted.description: True when the transition and its rule graph were removed.

discovery.summary: Bring a marketplace asset into the project: add a Fab listing, download a Fab asset, or import a Megascans asset.
whenToUse: marketplace=fab_listing: A Fab listing id is known and its content must be added to the project through the signed-in Fab tab.
marketplace=fab_download: A signed Fab download URL is in hand and the pack must be fetched to disk; it lands in the Fab cache, not in /Game.
marketplace=megascans: A Megascans pack already downloaded by Bridge must be imported with its master materials and presets applied.
whenNotToUse: marketplace=fab_listing: The listing must first be found or judged (use asset.query_marketplace).
marketplace=fab_listing: The pack is already downloaded on disk and only needs copying in (use asset.maintain_content with maintenance=migrate).
marketplace=fab_download: Only a listing id is known, with no signed URL (use marketplace=fab_listing, which adds the listing directly).
marketplace=fab_download: Downloads already on disk must be listed, not fetched again (use asset.query_marketplace).
marketplace=megascans: The Megascans library index must be browsed first (use asset.query_marketplace).
marketplace=megascans: The pack files should just be copied in as they are (use asset.maintain_content with maintenance=migrate).

listingId.description: Fab listing uid, as it appears in a fab.com/listings/<uid> URL. Restricted to [A-Za-z0-9_-], 64 characters max, because it is used to build an API path.

assetId.description: Fab asset id, used as the cache key.

downloadUrl.description: Signed https download URL issued by Fab. Short-lived: a stale URL fails with DOWNLOAD_FAILED.

destinationDirectory.description: Where the pack lands. Defaults to the Fab library cache directory, which list_fab_downloads and the fabLibrary source root both read.

downloadType.description: Transfer mode: "http" or "buildpatch". BuildPatchServices is for Marketplace-era packs; pointing it at a plain URL stalls rather than failing, so it must be opted into.

payload.description: A complete Bridge export envelope: { exportPayload: [ { assetId, assetType, exportMode, exportType, folderName, name, assetPaths[] } ] }. Use this to pass through exactly what Bridge would have sent.

assetPaths.description: Absolute paths of the downloaded pack files. Used with folderName to synthesize a single-entry envelope when payload is omitted.

folderName.description: Destination folder name under /Game/Megascans. Required when synthesizing from assetPaths.

assetType.description: Bridge asset type: 3d, 3dplant, atlas or surface.

exportMode.description: Bridge export mode: normal, normal_drag or progressive.

name.description: Display name. Defaults to folderName.

marketplace.description: Which import marketplace asset variant to run.

success.description: True only when assets actually appeared in the registry.

accepted.description: True when Fab accepted the workflow. Not the same as content existing.

assetCount.description: New assets the registry gained during the import.

importedRoot.description: Where the pack landed, chosen by Fab (typically /Game/<PackName>).

engineExactMatch.description: False when no listing version declared the running engine and the first version was used instead.

versionName.description: Listing version selected for this engine.

sampleAssetPaths.description: Up to ten imported asset paths, as registry evidence.

note.description: How to relocate the imported tree.

servedFromCache.description: True when the pack was already cached and no transfer occurred.

entryCount.description: Export-payload entries dispatched to the importer.

discovery.summary: Inspect an asset: metadata, what it uses or what uses it (referencers), its dependency graph, an exists-and-loads check, or a directory report.
whenToUse: lookup=metadata: What was recorded on an asset must be read back: its registry tags and the package metadata that asset.set_metadata writes, tags included (a tag set with kind=tags shows under metadata as "true").
lookup=dependencies: Before deleting or replacing an asset, the packages, Blueprints and levels that use it must be listed.
lookup=dependencies: The packages an asset itself uses must be listed (direct ones only).
lookup=graph: The reference graph of an asset must be walked several levels deep in one call (depth is capped at 8).
lookup=validate: An asset must be confirmed to exist and load before other calls rely on it (no content, reference or data checks are run).
lookup=report: Every asset under a directory, with name, path and class, must be listed in one reply, optionally saved as a JSON file in the project.
whenNotToUse: lookup=metadata: The asset's own values are wanted, such as a texture size or material parameters (use texture.get_texture_info or material.get_material_info).
lookup=dependencies: The node graph inside a material or Blueprint is wanted, not package links (use asset.query_asset with lookup=graph).
lookup=graph: Only the direct packages an asset uses, or the packages that use it, are needed (use lookup=dependencies, which is cheaper).
lookup=graph: A material's package references are wanted; a plain material answers here with its expression nodes (use lookup=dependencies).
lookup=validate: Every asset in a folder must be checked for load errors (use system_control.validate_assets).
lookup=report: A paged view of one folder is enough (use asset.list); the report returns the whole tree unpaged.

referencers.description: List the packages that USE this asset (Blueprints that spawn it, levels that place it) instead of the ones it uses; check this before deleting or replacing an asset.

lookup.description: Which inspect asset variant to run.

tags.description: Asset Registry tags (key-value). A tag written by set_tags appears here only when its name is listed under Project Settings > Asset Manager > Metadata Tags For Asset Registry.

metadata.description: Package metadata (key-value): what set_metadata wrote, and each set_tags tag as its name with the value "true".

details.description: Operation details.

graph.description: Adjacency map of asset path -> array of dependency paths.

maxDepth.description: Traversal depth actually used after clamping.

truncated.description: True when the walk hit the depth or node ceiling and the graph is partial.

examples.title: Inspect an asset: metadata, what it uses or what uses it (referencers), its dependency graph, an exists-and-loads check, or a directory report.

discovery.summary: List the assets and subfolders in a folder (path), the registered content sources, or the instances of a material.
whenToUse: kind=assets: what a folder holds must be seen (subfolders included unless recursive is false).
kind=content_sources: which template, feature pack, plugin or Fab folders exist to copy content from.
kind=material_instances: which material instances use a parent material.
whenNotToUse: An asset must be found by name, class or tag anywhere in the project (use query_asset).

offset.description: Zero-based offset into the full result set.
Zero-based offset into the full result set.

pagination.description: Nested pagination envelope. Top-level limit/offset take precedence when both are supplied.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned by a previous list response. Forward verbatim to resume.

recursive.description: Include the assets of every subfolder (default true); false lists only this folder's own assets, its subfolders still named under folders.

includeTags.description: When true, include asset tags in the listing response.

includeMetadata.description: When true, include the file size and modification date of each asset.

filter.description: Substring filter. Listing assets: a case-insensitive match on the asset name. Listing content sources: a case-sensitive match on the source id and, for plugins, the category.

sourceRoot.description: Restrict the listing to one root. One of: engineTemplates | engineFeaturePacks | engineContent | enginePlugins | megascansLibrary | fabLibrary | projectContent | projectPlugins. Omit to list every root.

includePackageCounts.description: Include packageCount per source. Costs a recursive file scan per returned entry, so leave off for a broad sweep and turn on once the candidate list is short.

kind.description: Which list variant to run; omit for 'assets'.

hasMore.description: True when more results exist beyond the current page.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the current page, or null when the page was requested without one.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null on the last page.

sources.description: Discovered sources. Each entry carries sourceRoot, sourceId, kind (template | featurePack | megascansPack | plugin | contentFolder), hasContentFolder, migratable, and packageCount when requested.

rootDirectories.description: Absolute directory each root token resolved to, so an operator can confirm where the Bridge library was found.

missingRoots.description: Root tokens whose directory does not exist on this machine.

details.description: Operation details.

discovery.summary: Content maintenance: bulk-rename assets, fix up redirectors, refresh the nodes of every Blueprint in a folder, or migrate packages from another content source.
whenToUse: maintenance=bulk_rename: A naming convention must be enforced across a folder or a list, such as swapping a prefix or adding a suffix to every asset.
maintenance=bulk_rename: Several unrelated assets must each get a specific new name in one call (the renames list).
maintenance=fixup_redirectors: Redirectors left in a folder by earlier moves or renames must be resolved: referencers are repointed and the redirectors deleted.
maintenance=refresh_blueprints: Blueprints in a folder or a list need every node refreshed, then compiled and saved, for example after a class was renamed.
maintenance=migrate: Loose .uasset content from an engine template, plugin or downloaded Fab or Megascans pack must be copied into the project.
maintenance=migrate: A migration must be previewed with a dry run before any file is copied.
whenNotToUse: maintenance=bulk_rename: One asset or one folder gets a new name (use asset.rename).
maintenance=fixup_redirectors: Redirectors should only be listed before anything changes (use asset.query_asset with lookup=search and classNames ObjectRedirector).
maintenance=refresh_blueprints: One Blueprint only needs compiling (use blueprint.compile).
maintenance=migrate: A source file (FBX, PNG, WAV) must become an asset (use asset.import).
maintenance=migrate: The available sources are still unknown (use asset.list with kind=content_sources).

pattern.description: Search pattern (used when searchText is absent).

replacement.description: Replacement text (used when replaceText is absent).

checkoutFiles.description: Check out files in source control.

renames.description: Explicit renames, each asset to its own new name in its own folder, all in this one call: [{sourcePath, newName}]. An entry whose asset is missing, or whose newName is taken, is skipped and named under skipped. Replaces the pattern fields.

sourceRoot.description: Content source root token. One of: engineTemplates | engineFeaturePacks | engineContent | enginePlugins | megascansLibrary | fabLibrary | projectContent | projectPlugins. A filesystem path is never accepted here — the token is resolved plugin-side, so no directory outside these roots is reachable. megascansLibrary probes both the shell Documents folder and the profile Documents folder (OneDrive redirects the first) and honours MCP_MEGASCANS_LIBRARY_DIR; fabLibrary reads the Fab plugin's own UFabSettings.CacheDirectoryPath and honours MCP_FAB_LIBRARY_DIR. The Fab plugin owns its own sign-in and downloading — these roots only read what it already placed on disk.

sourceId.description: Relative id under sourceRoot, exactly as returned by list_content_sources (for example "TP_VehicleAdvBP"). Must be relative: no "..", no leading "/", no drive prefix. Omit to migrate the root itself.

subPath.description: Optional folder under the source content directory, to migrate one subtree instead of the whole pack.

destinationPath.description: Root the copied tree lands under. Leave at "/Game" to preserve the source layout and keep internal references valid; any deeper path relocates the tree and flags referenceIntegrity as "at-risk".

overwrite.description: Overwrite packages that already exist at the destination. Default false, which skips them and reports skippedCount.

dryRun.description: Report what would be copied without writing anything. Returns the same counts and packagePaths sample.

maxPackages.description: Refuse the migration when the source holds more files than this, so a mistyped source cannot copy tens of gigabytes. Narrow with subPath or raise deliberately.

maintenance.description: Which maintain content variant to run.

details.description: Operation details.

sourceDirectory.description: Absolute directory the packages were read from.

copiedCount.description: Files copied (or that would be copied under dryRun).

skippedCount.description: Files already present at the destination and left alone because overwrite was false.

failedCount.description: Files that could not be copied.

totalFiles.description: Package files discovered in the source.

referenceIntegrity.description: "preserved" when the source layout was reproduced under /Game, "at-risk" when destinationPath relocated it.

packagePaths.description: Up to 40 destination package paths, for verifying the migration landed where expected.

failedFiles.description: Up to 20 source-relative paths that failed to copy.

warnings.description: Advisory messages, including the reference-integrity warning for a relocated destination.

examples.title: Content maintenance: bulk-rename assets, fix up redirectors, refresh the nodes of every Blueprint in a folder, or migrate packages from another content source.

sourcePath.description: Source /Game asset path, or a folder: everything under it moves into destinationPath, keeping sub-folders, and the emptied folder is removed.

newName.description: Rename in place instead: the asset keeps its folder and takes this name (used when destinationPath is omitted).

discovery.summary: Query assets: existence, search by name/class, find by tag, find where a text appears inside assets, the node graph inside a material or Blueprint, material stats, source-control state.
whenToUse: lookup=exists: A path must be tested for an asset, or several paths at once, before creating, importing or referencing one.
lookup=search: Assets must be found across the project by name, class, folder or asset-registry tag.

lookup=by_tag: Assets under /Game must be found by an asset-registry tag, optionally with one value, such as the ParentClass tag every Blueprint carries. A tag written by asset.set_metadata with kind=tags is in the registry only when its name is listed under Project Settings > Asset Manager > Metadata Tags For Asset Registry and the asset has been saved; otherwise nothing matches (asset.inspect_asset lookup=metadata reads one asset).
lookup=text: A piece of text, such as a UI label or dialogue line, must be traced to the Blueprint, widget, table row or level actor holding it.
lookup=graph: A material or Blueprint must be summarised: node counts, parameters, blend mode or graph count.
lookup=material_stats: A material's shading model, blend mode, domain, node and parameter counts, or the input pins its Main result node accepts, must be read.
lookup=source_control_state: Before editing, it must be known whether assets are checked out, modified or held by someone else.
whenNotToUse: lookup=exists: A folder's contents must be browsed rather than one path tested (use asset.list).
lookup=search|by_tag: Actors placed in the open level must be found (use control_actor.find).
lookup=text: One known Blueprint graph must be read node by node (use blueprint.inspect_graph).
lookup=graph: One Blueprint's variables, functions or components are wanted (use blueprint.get_blueprint).
lookup=material_stats: The individual nodes of a material and their connections are needed (use material.get_material_info).
lookup=source_control_state: Assets must be checked out or submitted (use asset.source_control).

assetPaths.description: Several asset paths checked in one call; the reply maps each to true or false under existsByPath.

classNames.description: Asset classes to filter: a short class name (StaticMesh, Blueprint, ObjectRedirector, InputMappingContext) or a full class path (/Script/Engine.StaticMesh).

offset.description: Zero-based offset into the full result set.

tag.description: Asset-registry tag name, for example ParentClass, which every Blueprint carries.

value.description: Optional tag value to match, ignoring case.

includeLevel.description: Also search the actors and components of the open level (default true).

recursive.description: Also report every /Game package the assets depend on, transitively (up to 512).

lookup.description: Which query asset variant to run.

details.description: Operation details.

hasMore.description: True when more results exist beyond the current page.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the current page, or null when the page was requested without one.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null on the last page.

matches.description: Each match: asset, where (graph and node title, widget, row, string key or actor label), field, the full text, and nodeId for a graph literal.

matchCount.description: Every match found; more than the matches returned when truncated.

scannedAssets.description: Blueprints, DataTables and String Tables searched.

truncated.description: True when limit cut the list; raise limit to see the rest.

assetClass.description: Concrete UClass name of the analyzed asset.

graphType.description: Graph kind analyzed: Material, Blueprint, or None.

nodeCount.description: Material expression nodes in the graph.

parameterCount.description: Material parameter expressions in the graph.

textureSampleCount.description: Texture sample expressions in the graph.

isMaterialInstance.description: True when the asset is a material instance.

isTwoSided.description: True when the material renders two-sided.

isMasked.description: True when the material uses masked blending.

blueprintType.description: Blueprint kind: Class, Interface, MacroLibrary, or FunctionLibrary.

totalNodes.description: Total nodes across every Blueprint graph.

graphCount.description: Number of graphs in the Blueprint.

message.description: Explanation when the asset type carries no graph.

examples.title: Query assets: existence, search by name/class, find by tag, find where a text appears inside assets, the node graph inside a material or Blueprint, material stats, source-control state.

discovery.summary: Query marketplace libraries: Fab listing details, Fab downloads, Fab library, Fab search, Megascans library.
whenToUse: lookup=fab_listing_details: A Fab search hit must be judged before adding it: description, seller, file formats and whether the project can import it.
lookup=fab_downloads: It must be known which Fab packs are already downloaded to this machine and where they are cached.
lookup=fab_library: The Fab listings the signed-in account owns must be listed, each with an id for adding to the project (needs a prior library sync).
lookup=fab_search: Content must be found on Fab by keyword, optionally free listings only, to get listing ids.
lookup=megascans_library: The Megascans packs downloaded by Bridge on this machine must be listed before one is imported.
whenNotToUse: lookup=fab_listing_details: The listing is chosen and must be added to the project (use asset.import_marketplace_asset with marketplace=fab_listing).
lookup=fab_downloads: A downloaded pack must be copied into the project (use asset.maintain_content with maintenance=migrate).
lookup=fab_library: A listing from the library is ready to add to the project (use asset.import_marketplace_asset with marketplace=fab_listing).
lookup=fab_search: Content already installed in an engine template, plugin or Bridge folder is wanted (use asset.list with kind=content_sources).
lookup=megascans_library: A listed pack should be imported into the project (use asset.import_marketplace_asset with marketplace=megascans).

listingId.description: Fab listing uid. Restricted to [A-Za-z0-9_-], 64 characters max.

columnTypes.description: Column struct paths to read, for example "/Script/Fab.FabObjectNameColumn". Defaults to the name column plus "/Script/Fab.FabObjectColumn", which carries AssetId, ListingType, Seller and Source. Selecting a column is also the row filter, so naming one Fab does not write for every row will hide rows. Override this when a Fab update renames or adds columns; unresolved paths are reported rather than failing the call.

filter.description: Case-sensitive substring matched against each serialized row. Use "fab" to drop the legacy "uem" engine and plugin entries that otherwise fill the row limit.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return, clamped plugin-side.

query.description: Free-text search. At most 128 characters, and no quotes, backslashes or control characters.

lookup.description: Which query marketplace variant to run.

imageBase64.description: Preview image bytes, base64. Promoted to an MCP image content block.

hasImage.description: False when no preview could be inlined.

imageOmitted.description: Present when the preview was skipped for exceeding the reply cap.

descriptionKeys.description: Listing keys observed when no description field matched.

thumbnailShape.description: Thumbnail keys observed when no image URL matched.

assetFormats.description: Asset format codes this listing ships, e.g. unreal-engine, fbx, gltf.

hasUnrealBuild.description: True when the listing ships a packaged unreal-engine build, which Fab imports through its pack workflow.

canAddToProject.description: True when add_fab_asset_to_project can actually import this listing. unreal-engine, gltf, glb and fbx are importable through the pack and Interchange workflows. Quixel/Megascans listings are the exception: Fab will not serve their download until the listing is claimed, and the claim is CSRF-protected with no token exposed to the page, so this reports false and addBlockedReason says so. Check this rather than hasUnrealBuild before adding.

addBlockedReason.description: Present when canAddToProject is false: why this listing cannot be imported.

downloads.description: Cached Fab downloads. Each entry carries assetId and cachedFile.

cacheDirectory.description: Directory the Fab plugin caches downloads in.

cacheDirectoryExists.description: False when nothing has been downloaded yet.

fabModuleAvailable.description: True when the plugin was built against the Fab module and read the cache through its own API rather than scanning the directory.

note.description: Guidance on what to do next given the current state.

entries.description: Library rows. Each entry maps column struct name to that column's properties, read by reflection. FabObjectColumn.AssetId is the listing id add_fab_asset_to_project takes.

unresolvedColumnTypes.description: Requested column paths that do not exist in this build — usually a Fab schema change.

listings.description: Matched listings: listingId, title, listingType, isFree (derived from price), rawIsFree (the listing flag, which disagrees), tags, and unresolvedPriceShape when price could not be read.

assets.description: Indexed library entries, verbatim from uassetsData.json.

indexExists.description: False when Bridge has never written an index here.

importAvailable.description: True when this build links the MegascansPlugin module, so import_megascans_asset can run.

examples.title: Query marketplace libraries: Fab listing details, Fab downloads, Fab library, Fab search, Megascans library.

discovery.summary: Rename an asset or a folder in place (newName), or move it (destinationPath); a folder takes every asset under it along. Several unrelated assets in one call: maintain_content bulk_rename with renames.
whenToUse: An asset needs a new name in its own folder; settings that point at it (default map, game mode) follow.
A folder must get a new name and every asset under it must go along.
whenNotToUse: Many assets need new names by pattern, prefix, suffix or a list (use asset.maintain_content with maintenance=bulk_rename).
A copy under a new name is wanted, with the original kept (use asset.duplicate).

sourcePath.description: Source /Game asset path, or a folder: a folder is renamed with everything under it.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Rename an asset or a folder in place (newName), or move it (destinationPath); a folder takes every asset under it along. Several unrelated assets in one call: maintain_content bulk_rename with renames.

discovery.summary: Set asset metadata key/values or asset tags.
whenToUse: kind=metadata: Key and value notes such as author or revision must be attached to an asset; the change stays unsaved until the asset is saved.
kind=tags: Simple labels such as Reviewed or Prop must be attached to an asset as package metadata; the change stays unsaved until the asset is saved.
whenNotToUse: kind=metadata: The stored values must be read back (use asset.inspect_asset).
kind=metadata: A property of the asset itself must change (use inspect.set_property).
kind=tags: Actors in a level need a tag (use control_actor.add_tag).

kind=tags: Assets must be found by the tag afterwards. asset.query_asset lookup=by_tag reads the asset registry, which carries a package-metadata tag only when its name is listed under Project Settings > Asset Manager > Metadata Tags For Asset Registry and the asset has been saved; otherwise it finds nothing.
kind=tags: The tags on an asset must be read back (use asset.inspect_asset lookup=metadata, which lists them under metadata at once).

tags.description: Tag names to set; each is written as package metadata with the value "true".

kind.description: Which set metadata variant to run; omit for 'metadata'.

details.description: Operation details.

discovery.summary: Revision control: initialise a repository, enable a provider, check out, submit, or commit every change.
whenToUse: sourceControlOp=checkout: Assets must be checked out of revision control before they are edited.
sourceControlOp=submit: Checked-out assets must be submitted to the revision-control server with a change description.
sourceControlOp=enable: A revision-control provider such as Git or Perforce must be selected before checkout or submit can work.
sourceControlOp=init: A project with no repository needs one, with an Unreal .gitignore and a first commit, in one call.
sourceControlOp=commit_all: A snapshot of every change in the project is wanted as one commit, for example after a batch of edits.
whenNotToUse: sourceControlOp=checkout: The checked-out or modified state of assets is wanted (use asset.query_asset for source control state).
sourceControlOp=submit|commit_all: Unsaved editor changes must reach disk first (use control_editor.save_all).
sourceControlOp=submit: Every change in the project is wanted as one Git snapshot, without listing assets (use sourceControlOp=commit_all).
sourceControlOp=enable: Only the state of particular assets is wanted (use asset.query_asset for source control state).
sourceControlOp=init: A Perforce or Subversion provider is wanted; init builds only a Git repository (select the provider with sourceControlOp=enable).
sourceControlOp=commit_all: Only chosen assets must go in, or the project uses Perforce or Subversion (use sourceControlOp=submit).

provider.description: Provider name as the editor registers it, e.g. Git or Perforce. Omit to report the current provider without changing it.

userName.description: Commit author name, written to the repository config only.

userEmail.description: Commit author email, written to the repository config only.

sourceControlOp.description: Which source control variant to run.

details.description: Operation details.

examples.title: Revision control: initialise a repository, enable a provider, check out, submit, or commit every change.

discovery.summary: Edit a Blueprint graph: add or create nodes (including reroute and struct make/break nodes), connect pins, set node properties and pin defaults, add a construction script, or run many of those edits, variables included, in one batch.
whenToUse: edit=add_node: A node must be added using a friendly type alias (e.g. Branch, Cast, GetVariable).
edit=create_node: A new node must be placed in a Blueprint event or function graph.
edit=create_reroute_node: Wire paths need a reroute node for cleaner layout.

edit=connect_pins: An exec or data link between two existing nodes must be created.
edit=set_node_property: A node-level property (e.g. comment, position) must be updated.
edit=set_pin_default_value: A pin's default literal value must be set when it has no incoming link.
edit=set_pin_default_value: A read-only text, string, name or number pin (TextRender Set Text's Value) needs a literal.
edit=add_construction_script: The Construction Script graph must be created or opened for editing.
edit=batch: More than a couple of nodes or links must be added to one Blueprint graph.
edit=batch: A new function and the nodes inside it must be built in one call.

For create_struct_make_break_nodes: make or break.

operations.description: Steps run in order, 1-200. Each is {edit, ...that edit's own params}. Member steps come before the nodes that use them: add_variable (variableName, variableType as add_variable takes it: basic, class, struct, enum and container types, defaultValue, isPublic, category), add_function (functionName, inputs, outputs, pure, isPublic; its body steps set graphName to the function name; with an id, "$id" is its entry node and "$id_return" its return node, which exists when outputs are declared), add_event (customEventName and parameters, or componentName plus eventName for a component or Widget Blueprint widget delegate, e.g. PlayButton with OnClicked) and add_event_dispatcher (dispatcherName, parameters [{name, type}]). Node steps: create_node, connect_pins, set_pin_default_value, set_node_property, create_reroute_node. create_node also takes nodeType CallDelegate (memberName: a dispatcher), Message (memberClass: an interface, memberName: its function), AsyncTask (memberClass: the task or async-action class, memberName: its static factory; event graphs only) and FunctionResult (one more return node in a function graph). Optional per step: id (names the created node; later steps use "$id" in fromNodeId, toNodeId and nodeId), from and to ("$id.PinName" shorthand for connect_pins), pinDefaults (create_node only: {PinName: value} applied to the new node; a read-only pin such as Set Text's Value gets a MakeLiteral node wired into it). "$entry" is the graph's own entry node (a Construction Script or function graph starts there: from "$entry.then"). A create step without posX and posY is auto-placed; one whose posX and posY overlap an existing node is placed at the nearest free position instead, and its result says where in placementWarning, so a crowded row never stops the batch (a single create_node call still refuses an overlap). Every function, variable, dispatcher and async factory a step names is checked before any step runs, so a misspelled one fails the batch with nothing applied; any other failure stops the batch at that step, and that step leaves nothing behind (a member step included), in whichever graph it ran.

estimatedHeight.description: Approximate node height, derived from pin-row count. Offset the next node by at least this much to avoid overlap.

overlappingNodes.description: Titles of existing nodes whose estimated bounds intersect this one. Empty or absent when placement is clear.

placementWarning.description: Human-readable overlap warning, present only when overlappingNodes is non-empty.

pinTypes.description: Per-pin objects: { name, direction, type, category, subCategory }.

compilerStatus.description: Blueprint status after compile (UpToDate, UpToDateWithWarnings, Error, Dirty, BeingCreated).

compiled.description: True when the Blueprint is up-to-date (warnings allowed).

connected.description: Whether the two pins are linked after the call, read back from the graph rather than inferred from the schema call.

targetPinName.description: Target pin that was actually used.

Each entry is an object with `type` plus that operation's own fields; `type: "add_component"` also takes componentName, componentClass, attachTo, transform, meshPath, materialPath and a nested properties bag; `type: "modify_component"` takes the same transform, meshPath, materialPath and properties for a component that already exists; transform is {location:{x,y,z}, rotation:{pitch,yaw,roll}, scale:{x,y,z}} (or those three directly on the operation), and a part left out keeps its current value; `type: "attach_component"` (or "reparent") moves componentName under parentComponent (or attachTo/newParent). A failed operation is named in warnings, and the call fails when none applied. Each result carries instancesUpdated (placed copies that took the change, 0 included) with up to three of their paths, and a hint, repeated in warnings, when a mesh or material lands on a hidden component.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

slotName.description: Slot name for a child widget inside its parent.

preset.description: Named anchor preset (e.g. TopCenter) applied in place of anchorMin/anchorMax.

size.description: Size override {x,y} of a CanvasPanel child. A HorizontalBox, VerticalBox or ScrollBox child is sized by sizeRule and fillValue instead.

sizeRule.description: A HorizontalBox, VerticalBox or ScrollBox child: Auto sizes it to its content, Fill shares the free space between the Fill children by their fillValue weights (case-insensitive). Two buttons in a row that should share it evenly are both Fill with the same fillValue; a ScrollBox child that is Fill spans the box when it is shorter, so a vertical alignment of center can center it.

fillValue.description: A HorizontalBox, VerticalBox or ScrollBox child: the Fill weight, 0 or more (1 by default; a child of 2 gets twice the space of a child of 1). Given without sizeRule it makes the child Fill.

alignment.description: CanvasPanel child: the pivot {x, y}, each 0-1. Any other slot (box, overlay, border, scroll box): x is the horizontal and y the vertical alignment, each a number (0 left/top, 0.5 center, 1 right/bottom) or a word: "fill", "left", "center", "right", "top", "bottom"; leave one out to keep it. {"x": "fill", "y": "center"} spans the width and centers vertically.

scale.description: Relative scale {x, y, z} for an SCS component template, or {x, y} for a widget render transform.

text.description: Text content for a text block or button.

texturePath.description: Texture asset path for an image or brush.

renderOpacity.description: Render opacity (0-1) applied to the widget and everything under it.

propertyName.description: Any other widget property, by reflection (such as WidgetStyle or Brush): read without value, written with it.

value.description: New value for propertyName: a string, number or bool, or an object or array for a struct property.

cornerRadius.description: Corner radius in pixels for a widget that draws a brush (Image, Button, Border). Switches the brush to a RoundedBox; 0 restores square corners.

outlineColor.description: Outline color (0-1 values) drawn around a rounded brush. Ignored unless cornerRadius is set.

outlineWidth.description: Outline thickness in pixels around a rounded brush. Ignored unless cornerRadius is set.

hoverSoundPath.description: Sound a Button plays when the pointer moves onto it (SoundCue, SoundWave or MetaSound path); an empty string clears it.

pressSoundPath.description: Sound a Button plays when it is pressed (SoundCue, SoundWave or MetaSound path); an empty string clears it.

justification.description: Text justification of a TextBlock or RichTextBlock: left, center or right. To centre the widget itself in its slot use set_alignment.

fontFamily.description: Font asset for a TextBlock, e.g. /Engine/EngineFonts/Roboto or a project font.

typeface.description: Face of the TextBlock font: Regular, Bold, Italic, Light... A face the font lacks is refused with the list it has.

letterSpacing.description: Extra space between the letters of a TextBlock, in thousandths of an em (0 normal, 100 airy, negative tighter).

copyStyleFrom.description: Name of another TextBlock in the same Widget Blueprint whose font, colour and shadow this one takes; the other fields in the call then apply on top.

layoutProperty.description: Which set widget layout variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

slotName.description: Slot name for a child widget inside its parent.

applied.description: The widget as it is now: visibility, renderOpacity, renderTransform, slotClass, and the canvas anchors, alignment, position, size, zOrder and autoSize or the box padding and horizontal and vertical alignment.

saved.description: Whether the Widget Blueprint was saved.

appliedFields.description: set_style: the style fields that were written (text, fontSize, colorAndOpacity, cornerRadius...).

discovery.summary: Sweep every actor in the level and report the ones that interpenetrate another actor, sit sunk below the surface under them, float above it, lean off vertical, or have a face in the same plane as another surface (z-fighting flicker).
whenToUse: A level was assembled programmatically and needs checking before anyone looks at it.
Actors appear to clip through each other, stand in the ground, or lie on their side.
A placement pass should be verified without flying the viewport around to eyeball it.

Surfaces flicker, or another material shows through in ragged patches (z-fighting): the coplanar face pairs responsible are listed under coplanarFaces, with the direction to push each one; control_actor fix_coplanar fixes them all in one call.
whenNotToUse: One actor was just moved; spawn and set_transform already return placementWarning for it.

A finding is a deliberate composition (a keep bedding its towers into its platform, an island meant to hang in the air, a signpost leaning by design): tag that actor mcp.placement.ok with control_actor.add_tag and it drops out of the sweep entirely -- as tilt subject, and as both subject and target for overlap -- rather than being re-reported every time. Coplanar faces are still reported for tagged actors, because they flicker whatever the intent.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

nameFilter.description: Only examine actors whose label contains this text. Omit to sweep the whole level.

limit.description: Maximum problem entries to return (1-200, default 25). Entries come worst-first, so a small limit still shows the placements that matter; flagged is always the true total.

minSeverity.description: Drop findings whose severity (worst penetration, ground error, tilt displacement, or the side of the largest z-fighting patch, in world units) is below this. Use it to skip cosmetic grazes on a large level.

kinds.description: Report only these problem kinds, e.g. ["coplanar"] to list z-fighting alone in a platformer full of platforms that float on purpose. An actor whose worst problem is another kind still counts for coplanar when it has coplanarFaces. Omit for every kind.

maxTilt.description: Degrees off vertical an actor may lean before it is reported as tilted (1-90, default 30). Lean is the angle between the up vector of the actor and world up, so yaw never counts and a fully inverted actor reads 180. Raise it for a level whose props are deliberately strewn about; lower it to catch subtler leans.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

flagged.description: Actors with a placement problem, before the limit.

byKind.description: Count of flagged actors per problem kind: sunk, floating, overlapping, unsupported, tilted, coplanar.

problems.description: Findings worst-first: actorName, kind, severity in world units, the issue in words, suggestedZ when a resting height can be computed, and coplanarFaces when faces z-fight: one entry per pair with direction (the axis both faces point along, e.g. -Y), component, otherActor, otherComponent, gap and overlapU x overlapV. Fix a pair by moving the face about 2 units along direction (this piece shows) or against it (the other shows, right for a piece sunk into it, such as a ramp in the floor), by moving or scaling the actor. Call get_actor_transform on one for its full detail.

truncationNote.description: Present when the limit cut the list short; says how to reach the rest.

examples.title: Sweep every actor in the level and report the ones that interpenetrate another actor, sit sunk below the surface under them, float above it, lean off vertical, or have a face in the same plane as another surface (z-fighting flicker).

discovery.summary: Fix z-fighting in one call: every actor with a face in the same plane as another surface moves a unit, so one surface is clearly in front, repeating until nothing is left to move. A piece lying wholly inside the other face (a door on a wall) comes forward; one only partly inside (a ramp sunk into the floor) goes back so the other shows. Two parts of one Blueprint actor are parted in the Blueprint itself, so every placed copy is fixed at once.
whenToUse: audit_placement reported coplanar faces, or surfaces flicker between two materials.
A level was built from boxes placed flush against each other and should be cleaned up before anyone looks at it.
whenNotToUse: Only some actors may move: limit the call with nameFilter. A tag of mcp.placement.ok does not exempt an actor, because no two faces flicker on purpose.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

nameFilter.description: Only fix pairs where either actor label contains this text. Omit for the whole level.

distance.description: How far each face moves, in world units (0.1-20, default 1): far enough for the depth buffer, too little to see.

dryRun.description: List the moves without making them (default false).

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

pairsFound.description: Coplanar face pairs found before fixing.

remainingPairs.description: Coplanar pairs still found afterwards; run audit_placement with kinds ["coplanar"] to see them.

passes.description: Passes made: a move can line an actor up with a neighbour that moved the same way, so the fix repeats (at most four passes; one under dryRun).

moved.description: One entry per actor: actorName, offset {x, y, z} it moved by, resized when both of its faces on one axis moved (for example "grew 2.0 units along X"), and pairs, each face with the other actor and whether it was brought forward or pulled back.

blueprintsFixed.description: Pairs inside one Blueprint actor, fixed in the Blueprint: which part moved off which, and where it now sits in every placed copy (the Blueprint is compiled and saved).

skipped.description: Pairs left alone, each with the reason and what to do instead.

examples.title: Fix z-fighting in one call: every actor with a face in the same plane as another surface moves a unit, so one surface is clearly in front, repeating until nothing is left to move. A piece lying wholly inside the other face (a door on a wall) comes forward; one only partly inside (a ramp sunk into the floor) goes back so the other shows. Two parts of one Blueprint actor are parted in the Blueprint itself, so every placed copy is fixed at once.

output.message: Would move 3 actors and 1 Blueprint parts in 1 passes for 4 coplanar pairs; 4 pairs remain

discovery.summary: Read an actor's transform now, or watch it over game time in PIE (motion): location, velocity and chosen properties at every interval, to prove a jump, launch, patrol or fall in one call.
whenToUse: readMode=transform: The current transform of an actor must be inspected.
readMode=motion: A jump, spring launch, moving platform, enemy patrol or fall must be proven in PIE without a sleep-and-poll loop.
readMode=motion: The peak height, landing point or path of a moving actor is needed.

readMode=motion: An input must land at an exact moment (jump when a platform appears): inputs and startWhen run the whole timeline inside one call, so the caller's own delay between calls cannot shift it.
whenNotToUse: readMode=transform: The transform should be changed (use set_transform).
readMode=motion: Nothing is playing: the editor world does not simulate (start PIE with control_editor.play).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

actorName.description: Target actor name in the current level; while PIE runs, PlayerPawn names the player's pawn (PlayerController, GameMode, GameState, PlayerState and HUD work too).

durationSeconds.description: Game seconds to watch (default 2, at most 30). Game time, so a clock slowed with set_game_speed still covers the same span of play; a run that needs more wall-clock time than maxRealSeconds stops there (endedBecause realTimeCap).

intervalSeconds.description: Game seconds between samples (default 0.05; 0 samples every frame). At most 400 samples are kept.

propertyNames.description: Actor properties read at every sample, e.g. ["bDead", "HP"], or a component's as "Component.Property" ("Visual.RelativeScale3D" catches a squash on landing); a name that resolves to nothing is listed under missingProperties.

maxRealSeconds.description: Wall-clock cap (default 25, at most 50): the run stops here and reports how much game time it covered, so a long run or an editor throttled to 3 fps still answers before a client that gives up at 30 s. Raise it only for a client that waits longer.

key.description: Key name as simulate_input takes it: SpaceBar, D, A, Left, Enter.

atSeconds.description: Game seconds after the run starts to press it (default 0).

inputs.description: Keys pressed and released at exact game times during the run (at most 32), e.g. [{"key":"D","atSeconds":0,"holdSeconds":2},{"key":"SpaceBar","atSeconds":0.6,"holdSeconds":0.2}]. A key still held when the run ends is released.

actorName.description: Actor whose property starts the run.

propertyName.description: That actor's property, as propertyNames reads it (e.g. bActorEnableCollision).

equals.description: Value that starts the run, as samples show it ("True", "False", 3).

waitForChange.description: Default true: start only when the value BECOMES equals (a platform appearing), not while it already is.

maxWaitSeconds.description: Game seconds to wait before giving up with endedBecause startWhenTimeout (default 10, at most 30).

startWhen.description: Hold the run (samples and inputs) until another actor's property takes a value, so the timeline starts on a game event instead of whenever the call arrived.

readMode.description: Which get transform variant to run; omit for 'transform'.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

location.description: World or relative location as [x, y, z].

rotation.description: Rotation as [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees.

actorName.description: The actor watched.

samples.description: One entry per sample: t (game seconds since the start), location [x, y, z], velocity [x, y, z], properties.

endedBecause.description: duration, realTimeCap, sampleCap, actorDestroyed (a PIE death that reloads the level ends here), worldEnded (PIE stopped) or startWhenTimeout (startWhen never happened within maxWaitSeconds).

inputsApplied.description: One entry per input: key, at, hold, and down/up, the game seconds since the start when it was pressed and released (up is when the run ended for a key still held).

waitedSeconds.description: Game seconds spent waiting for startWhen before the run began.

min.description: Smallest x, y and z sampled (the lowest point is min[2]).

max.description: Largest x, y and z sampled (the peak height is max[2]).

missingProperties.description: propertyNames the actor's class does not have.

windowRestored.description: True when the editor window was minimized: a minimized editor runs PIE at about 3 fps, so it was put back on screen, without taking focus, before the run.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

limit.description: Maximum number of actors to return in a list.

filter.description: Optional name substring filter for list.

offset.description: Skip this many matching actors; the next page starts at nextOffset from the previous reply.

tag.description: Only actors carrying this actor tag. With summary, shows what the tag covers before a delete_by_tag removes it.

className.description: Only actors of this class or a subclass, by name or path: TextRenderActor, Light (every light type), or a Blueprint such as BP_Sign, with or without _C.

folder.description: Only actors in this outliner folder or a folder under it (Level/Stage matches Level/Stage/Signs); "(none)" for the actors at the root.

propertyNames.description: Property or Blueprint variable names to read on every listed actor, returned per actor under properties, e.g. Kind and Content, or a component's as "Component.Property" (StaticMeshComponent.LDMaxDrawDistance, Visual.RelativeScale3D; the component by its name), keyed as asked. A name that an actor lacks, or whose component it lacks, is listed under missingProperties for that actor.

near.description: A world point as [x, y, z] (an {x, y, z} object works too): list what is close to it, nearest first, each row with its distance. radius.description: World units from near: an actor is listed when its bounding box comes within this distance of the point (the distance is 0 for a box that contains the point, such as a floor slab under it). Needs near.

actors.description: Matched actors; with near, nearest first, each with its distance.

totalCount.description: Listable actors matching the filter, before the limit is applied.

excludedCount.description: Actors present in the world but never listable here: templates, transient actors, the builder brush and WorldSettings. Explains why this total is below the actorCount get_editor_state reports for the same world.

worldName.description: Name of the active world (or PIE world) the actors were listed from.

name.description: Class, tag or folder.

discovery.summary: Call one reflected UFunction on a plugin's live object, marshalling arguments through the function's own property chain. No signature is hardcoded: whatever describe_reflected_api reports for the installed build is what this accepts, so an integration stays correct across plugin updates instead of silently passing a stale parameter list. Return and out parameters come back in `outputs`. Refuses when only the class default object exists, because invoking on the CDO mutates shared defaults and never reaches the running instance. This is arbitrary in-process invocation — it can reach any reflected function on any resolvable object — so it demands elevated consent.
whenToUse: A plugin exposes the needed operation only as a UFUNCTION and no native capability covers it.
describe_reflected_api confirmed the function and its current parameters.
whenNotToUse: A native capability already covers the operation — prefer it; a reflected call carries none of the safety wrappers, undo transactions, or path validation the domain handlers apply.
The signature has not been confirmed against the installed build.

discovery.summary: Capture a viewport screenshot, optionally from a camera location and rotation given in the same call.
whenToUse: A visual snapshot of the editor or game viewport is needed.
whenNotToUse: A real-time capture stream is needed.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

path.description: Directory to save the PNG in, inside the project (relative to it, or absolute under it). Default Saved/Screenshots (game_viewport: Saved/Screenshots/WindowsEditor). A path outside the project is refused.

resolution.description: Maximum WxH for the returned PNG (e.g. "1280x720"). The capture is downscaled to fit inside this box with its aspect ratio preserved; a box at least as large as the viewport leaves the image untouched. Without it an image returned inline fits 1600x900, and a file-only capture (returnBase64 false) keeps the viewport size.

mode.description: Screenshot source: editor_viewport (default, the level viewport), game_viewport (the running game frame WITHOUT any UMG widgets) or full_editor_window (the editor window as displayed: the only mode that shows game UI and asset editors).

window.description: With mode full_editor_window, which window to capture: a list index ("2") or a case-insensitive substring of its title ("WBP_HubUI"). Omit for the main editor frame, which is then always what is captured: a minimized main frame is restored without taking focus, and when that is not possible the call fails with EDITOR_WINDOW_MINIMIZED instead of capturing another window. Every response lists the open windows under windows[], so read that to pick one.

location.description: editor_viewport: put the level viewport camera here first, in the same call ({x, y, z}); it stays there. Ignored while Play In Editor runs (the game camera is captured).

rotation.description: editor_viewport: turn the level viewport camera to this first ({pitch, yaw, roll}), in the same call.

returnBase64.description: Return the PNG inline as an image (default true); a capture also saves a file unless keepFile is false. With no resolution, an inline image is downscaled to fit 1600x900. false returns only the saved path and metadata, at the full viewport size.

keepFile.description: false: hand the image back without leaving a file in Saved/Screenshots (refused with returnBase64 false, which would leave no output at all). Default true. Files already written are listed by system_control list_output_files and removed by delete_output_file.

includeMetadata.description: Attach caller-provided metadata to the response.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

width.description: Width in pixels of the PNG actually returned.

height.description: Height in pixels of the PNG actually returned.

viewportWidth.description: Width in pixels of the viewport (or, for full_editor_window, the window) the picture was taken at. Present only when the image was downscaled (a resolution, or the 1600x900 inline default), so width/height differ from it.

viewportHeight.description: Height in pixels of the viewport or window the picture was taken at. Present only when the image was downscaled.

window.description: Title of the editor window that was actually captured.

mainWindow.description: full_editor_window: true when the captured window is the main editor frame.

windows.description: Every visible editor window: index, title, x, y, width, height, isActive, isModal. Pass an index or a title substring back as the window parameter to capture a different one; x/y are screen coordinates for simulate_input.

cameraLocation.description: editor_viewport: where the camera was for this picture.

cameraRotation.description: editor_viewport: how the camera was turned for this picture.

discovery.summary: Simulate a keyboard or mouse input event (key_down, key_up, key_tap, mouse_click, mouse_move), or list and press the live UMG widgets of a PIE session (widget_list, widget_click).
whenToUse: Synthetic input must be injected into the editor or PIE.
A game has to be played: key_tap taps a key, key_down with holdSeconds holds it for that many game seconds, and inputAction injects an Enhanced Input action directly when no key is mapped to it.

A game UI must be operated in PIE: widget_list names every live widget, and widget_click presses a Button, toggles a CheckBox or sets a Slider (value) by name without touching the OS cursor, so it works while the editor window is in the background.
whenNotToUse: Real hardware input is available.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

key.description: Key name: SpaceBar, D, Left, Enter, P. Escape is the editor stop-play key: in Play In Editor it ends the session instead of reaching the game, so test an action bound to Escape through another key mapped to it.

type.description: Input event type (key_down, key_up, key_tap = press then release, mouse_click, mouse_move), or widget_list / widget_click to operate the live UMG of a PIE session.

inputType.description: Alias for type used by simulate_input.

inputAction.description: Enhanced Input action to inject directly, as an asset path such as /Game/Input/IA_Move. A raw key already reaches Enhanced Input through the active mapping contexts (key_down D moves a pawn whose context maps D); use inputAction when no key is mapped to the action, or to inject an analog value.

value.description: Scalar value to inject for inputAction (default 1; use a negative value for the opposite direction), or the value to set a Slider to with widget_click. Ignored for a raw key.

holdSeconds.description: Keep injecting inputAction, or keep a raw key_down/key_tap key pressed, for this many seconds of GAME time so the pawn actually travels (default 0: an action lasts one frame, a key_down stays down until key_up, a key_tap lets go after 0.1s). Game time, not wall time: under set_game_speed 0.05 a 2s hold still delivers 2s of in-game input, which takes 40s of real time. A key_up for the same action or key stops the hold early.

x.description: Mouse X coordinate for simulate_input, or the X value of an Axis2D or Axis3D inputAction.

y.description: Mouse Y coordinate for simulate_input, or the Y value of an Axis2D or Axis3D inputAction.

z.description: Z value of an Axis3D inputAction (x and y give the other two).

widget.description: For type widget_click: the live UMG widget to drive, by name (PlayButton), or Owner.Name (WBP_MainMenu.PlayButton) when several share it. widget_list shows both.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

routedToPIE.description: The event was routed to the PIE viewport rather than the editor.

handledByPIE.description: PIE actually consumed the event. False here with routedToPIE true means the key reached the game and nothing bound it: no active input mapping context maps that key (inject the action with inputAction instead).

injectedAction.description: The Enhanced Input action that was injected, when inputAction resolved to one. Absent means the call went down the raw-key path, which reaches the game only through a mapping context that maps the key.

widgets.description: widget_list: each live user widget (userWidget, object, inViewport) with its Button/CheckBox/Slider children (name, type, enabled, visible, focused, and text, value or checked).

widget.description: widget_click: the widget that was driven, as Owner.Name.

widgetType.description: widget_click: the driven widget's class (Button, CheckBox, Slider).

examples.title: Simulate a keyboard or mouse input event (key_down, key_up, key_tap, mouse_click, mouse_move), or list and press the live UMG widgets of a PIE session (widget_list, widget_click).

discovery.summary: Stop, pause or resume playing sounds: the 2D sounds play_sound started (only that sound with soundPath), or with all every sound the editor and a running game play, its music included. Pause holds a sound where it is and resume continues it; the reply counts the sounds changed (0 when none was playing).
whenToUse: soundOp=stop: Use it to stop sounds: the 2D sounds play_sound started (only that sound with soundPath), or with all every sound the editor and a running game play, its music included.
soundOp=pause: Use it to pause the sounds stop_sound would stop, each held where it is. Sounds already paused are not counted.
soundOp=resume: Use it to resume the paused sounds stop_sound would stop, each from where it was paused.
whenNotToUse: The game or the Play In Editor session must be paused (use control_editor pause).

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

all.description: Also act on every sound the editor and a running Play In Editor game play, game music included (default false: only the 2D sounds play_sound started). Stop silences every audio device; pause and resume take soundPath to narrow it to one sound.

soundOp.description: Which stop sound variant to run; omit for 'stop'.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

stopped.description: Sounds play_sound had started that this call stopped.

allStopped.description: Whether every sound on the editor and game audio devices was stopped (all: true).

paused.description: Playing sounds this call paused (0 when none was playing).

resumed.description: Paused sounds this call resumed (0 when none was paused).

discovery.summary: Create an interactable: door, chest, switch, lever or trigger actor, an interactable interface, or an interaction component.
whenToUse: kind=door: A door Blueprint is needed with a pivot, a door mesh and a trigger box, plus open-angle, timing, lock and key variables.
kind=chest: A chest Blueprint is needed with a base mesh, a lid mesh on a pivot, a trigger sphere and an optional locked state.
kind=switch|lever: A switch, button or lever needs an actor Blueprint with mesh parts and an overlap sphere as its trigger.
kind=trigger: A reusable overlap-volume Blueprint is needed with a box, sphere or capsule as its root shape.
kind=interface: A Blueprint interface is needed that defines Interact, CanInteract and GetInteractionPrompt for actors to implement.
kind=component: An existing Blueprint, such as a player, needs a named overlap sphere whose radius is the interaction range.
whenNotToUse: kind=door|chest|switch|lever|trigger: An actor must be placed in the level from an existing Blueprint (use control_actor.spawn).
kind=door|chest|switch: An existing door, chest or switch only needs new settings (use manage_interaction.configure_interactable).
kind=lever: Switch type, toggle and reset settings must be editable later, which only a switch Blueprint allows.

discovery.summary: Configure replication on a Blueprint: property replication and conditions, RepNotify, net role, dormancy, relevancy, priority, update frequency, cull distance, push model, replicated movement, replication graph, net driver.
whenToUse: setting=property: Use it to turn replication of a Blueprint variable on or off, optionally with its replication condition.
setting=condition: Use it to set a Blueprint property replication condition.
setting=rep_notify: Use it to assign a RepNotify function to a property.
setting=net_role: Use it to choose how clients see an Actor Blueprint's actors: ROLE_None turns replication off, ROLE_SimulatedProxy or ROLE_AutonomousProxy turn it on.
setting=dormancy: Use it to set an Actor Blueprint's default network dormancy.
setting=always_relevant: Use it to set always-relevant replication behavior.
setting=only_relevant_to_owner: Use it to set owner-only relevancy behavior.
setting=autonomous_proxy: Use it to make every replicated variable of a Blueprint replicate to the autonomous proxy only (COND_AutonomousOnly), or undo that; fails when it has no replicated variable.
setting=priority: Use it to configure actor network bandwidth priority.
setting=update_frequency: Use it to configure actor network update frequency.
setting=cull_distance: Use it to configure network relevancy cull distance.
setting=push_model: Use it to turn push-model replication on or off for every replicated variable of a Blueprint; fails when it has none.
setting=replicated_movement: Use it to configure replicated movement.
setting=replication_graph: Use it to set an Actor Blueprint's spatially loaded (World Partition) and net load on client defaults; only the fields sent are written.
setting=net_driver: Use it to write the game net driver's rate limits to its class defaults and DefaultEngine.ini, and to the running net driver when there is one; only the fields sent are written.

action.description: The action to execute on the parent tool.

condition.description: Replication condition, a ELifetimeCondition name such as COND_OwnerOnly, COND_SkipOwner, COND_InitialOnly or COND_AutonomousOnly; an unknown name is refused.

role.description: How clients see the actor: ROLE_None (not replicated), ROLE_SimulatedProxy or ROLE_AutonomousProxy (replicated). ROLE_Authority is refused: the server always has it.

dormancy.description: Net dormancy, a ENetDormancy name: DORM_Never, DORM_Awake, DORM_DormantAll, DORM_DormantPartial or DORM_Initial; an unknown name is refused.

isAutonomousProxy.description: true: every replicated variable replicates to the autonomous proxy only (COND_AutonomousOnly). false: variables using COND_AutonomousOnly go back to COND_None; other conditions stay.

spatiallyLoaded.description: World Partition: stream the actor in by distance (AActor bIsSpatiallyLoaded).

netLoadOnClient.description: Load the placed actor on clients with the map (AActor bNetLoadOnClient).

maxClientRate.description: Game net driver MaxClientRate (bytes per second per LAN client).

maxInternetClientRate.description: Game net driver MaxInternetClientRate (bytes per second per internet client).

netServerMaxTickRate.description: Game net driver NetServerMaxTickRate (server ticks per second).

setting.description: Which configure replication variant to run.

details.description: Additional handler result fields not named by the contract.

examples.title: Configure replication on a Blueprint: property replication and conditions, RepNotify, net role, dormancy, relevancy, priority, update frequency, cull distance, push model, replicated movement, replication graph, net driver.
